case.title: RFQ: pump shaft for the new HX series

claims: Our bottom-up should-cost estimate for this part is EUR 36.87 per unit (cost:320070).
Electricity producer prices changed -6.1% from 2025-11 to 2026-08 (idx:PPI-D351@2025-11, idx:PPI-D351@2026-08).
The 1.4404 alloy surcharge changed -5.5% from 2026-06 to 2026-09 (idx:AS-14404@2026-06, idx:AS-14404@2026-09).
Producer prices for cold-drawn bars changed -2.3% from 2026-06 to 2026-08 (idx:PPI-C2431@2026-06, idx:PPI-C2431@2026-08).

economics: The current price (€36.39) is €0.48 per unit (1.3%) below the should-cost estimate (€36.87), so the estimate does not show price above cost or clear price-reduction room.
The listed cost-driver weights total 76%; their weighted 12-month contribution is about +4.1%, but the missing 24% and lack of price history prevent judging whether they justify the supplier’s price.
The supplier letter gives no price, and the data gives no lead time or competing quotes to quantify further price room.
persona: The owner appears influential, but the office manager handles costing; final approval authority is not stated.
Capacity may be available: sales said they could take extra parts at short notice, and the second shift is on hold.
Hollerau is an important reference customer to Dralveck, giving the relationship potential value to them.
Dr alveck complained of overdue invoices, though our records show we pay 8.4 days early on average; no evidence identifies price freezes.
history: Across six comparable negotiations, Dralveck settled an average 2.1 percentage points below its ask; settlements averaged a 1.6% price decrease.
The contract fixes prices by calendar year and requires 90 days’ written notice for changes; it specifies 30-day payment (with 2% discount within 10 days) and a 28-day standard lead time.
The RFQ names three suppliers, but gives no supplier-specific sourcing or capacity data; without a deal, demand is bought at the fallback price, so relative dependence cannot be established.
leverage: On-time delivery fell from 85.7% in 2025Q4 to 80.8% in 2026Q3, supporting a push for better terms.
Defects were high in every reported quarter (1,214–1,997 ppm), another basis to seek improved terms.
The next-12-month forecast rose from 450 units in 2026-03 to 2,390 in 2026-09, giving the supplier a larger potential opportunity.

strategy.notes: Dralveck is an established supplier with potential capacity, but its delivery and defect performance gives us a credible basis to seek better overall terms. Acknowledge the larger HX opportunity and our reliable payment record, while grounding any price request in the modest outcomes of comparable negotiations rather than unsupported cost or competitor claims.
strategy.reason: The evidence supports a firm, factual approach, but limited demonstrated price room and modest historical concessions do not justify opening closer to the quote or departing from the usual move size.

economics: The current price (€36.39) is €0.48, or about 1.3%, below the should-cost estimate (€36.87); this indicates no clear price-down room on the cost estimate alone, whose confidence is only 10%.

The listed cost drivers contribute a weighted increase of about 4.1 percentage points over 12 months, but their weights total only 76%; the data therefore do not establish whether the price is justified overall.
No useful price-history or supplier-quotation comparison is provided.
persona: Hrvelec’s order book is full beyond six months and it will confirm extra volume only with a binding 12-month commitment, so capacity and commitment are key decision factors.
The 12-month commitment could secure capacity, but conflicts with your two-year horizon and limits flexibility.
history: In the last three negotiations, two supplier price increases were settled at 0%; in the latest, the settlement was 2.1 percentage points below the supplier’s ask.
The recorded contract sets 45-day payment and 42-day standard lead time, with annual fixed prices and 90 days’ notice for price changes.
The contract scope is for a machined flange, not a pump shaft, so its terms may not apply to this RFQ.
The data does not establish either side’s sourcing dependence; three suppliers are named for the RFQ, but no competing offers or sourcing shares are provided.
leverage: Latest on-time delivery was only 62.5%, and defects were 980 ppm, supporting a lower price or stronger delivery and quality terms.
Performance has improved from 80.0% on-time delivery and 2,260 ppm defects in 2025Q4, which supports the supplier’s case.
The 12-month forecast rose from 450 units in March 2026 to 2,390 in September 2026, indicating growing potential demand for the supplier.
No rival quotes or lead-time data are provided.

strategy.notes: Hrvelec is capacity-constrained and needs a firm commitment before confirming additional volume, so avoid implying we can guarantee more than our demand outlook supports. We can share the growing potential demand and raise its documented delivery and quality performance, while being clear that the prior contract history may not apply to this shaft.
strategy.reason: A modestly less aggressive opening reflects the supplier’s full order book and uncertain cost-down room, while a standard move size suits a supplier likely to make few counters.

economics: At €36.39, the price is €0.48 (1.3%) below the €36.87 should-cost estimate; that estimate has only 10% confidence.

Available cost drivers point upward: their weighted contributions total +4.1 percentage points, but they cover only 76% of the stated weights, so they do not establish a specific justified price increase.
The data shows little cost-based room to push below the current price; no supplier price history or comparable competing quotes are provided to quantify further room.
persona: No specific decision-maker or approval process is identified; the company is founder-owned.
Cash matters: they asked for payment within 10 days in exchange for a discount and warned that repeated late payment could lead them to review conditions.
They have free capacity, have paused hiring and a second shift, and say they can take additional parts at short notice.
Hollerau is an important reference customer to them; no frozen-price position is mentioned.
history: Across three renewals, settlements were 1.3 percentage points more favorable to Hollerau than the supplier’s ask each time.
The contract fixes annual prices; changes require 90 days’ written notice before year-end. It also sets 30-day payment and a 28-day standard lead time.
The contract scope is a spacer sleeve, not a pump shaft, so its terms may not apply to this RFQ.
leverage: On-time delivery fell from 95.8% in 2026Q1 to 88.0% in 2026Q3, supporting a request for better delivery terms.
Defects improved from 496 ppm in 2026Q1 to 318 ppm in 2026Q3, supporting the supplier’s case.
The forecast rose from 450 to 2,390 units over the next 12 months, supporting the supplier’s case for the business opportunity.

strategy.notes: This founder-owned supplier has spare capacity and values Hollerau as a reference customer, while cash flow matters to them. We can point to the history of favorable settlements cautiously, since it concerns a different part, and raise delivery performance constructively; offer reliable, timely payment and the opportunity for additional business without promising terms we cannot meet.
strategy.reason: Use a standard measured opening and concession pace: spare capacity and past settlements offer some leverage, but the cost evidence is weak, the contract history is not directly comparable, and no competing quotes quantify further price room.

events.notes: Jana Procházková, Export Manager at Strojírna Hrvelec, has made an opening offer and signals room to move. She values a long-term partnership; respond warmly and invite her to improve the offer.

events.body:
Dear Sir or Madam,

Thank you for your offer and for the time your team has put into it.
We understand that your capacity is fully committed and that a firm volume commitment matters; the binding volume below represents our full demand for this part over the term, all placed with you. We value the opportunity to build a long-term relationship with you—could you improve your offer on this basis?

We confirm a binding volume of 4200 units a year for the 24-month term, our full demand for this part, all placed with you.

Your on-time delivery was 62.5% in 2026Q3 (sc:70240@2026Q3).
Electricity producer prices changed -6.1% from 2025-11 to 2026-08 (idx:PPI-D351@2025-11, idx:PPI-D351@2026-08).

On this basis we propose: EUR 30.51 per unit, payment 14 days net, lead time 42 days, for our full demand of 4200 units a year over 24 months.

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke, Purchasing
